# Writing Sample 01 — "Eagle of Alamut" Ch. 1 (human-written, craft reference only)

> Source: teecup_angel, *Eagle of Alamut* (Assassin's Creed), AO3 work 44196343.
> Kept ONLY as a style reference for prose rhythm, paragraph length, internal-voice cadence,
> how canon is woven in quietly, and how emotion is carried. Study the craft; never copy the
> words, names, characters, or plot into a generated story.

## Why this is the target voice

- Paragraphs are tiny. Many are a single line. Single words sit on their own line for rhythm.
- The internal voice is tired, wry, practical, and profane where it fits the character. Desmond
  sounds like Desmond: unsure but confident, thrown off by being sixteen again.
- Canon is everywhere but never shouted. The Bleeding Effect, the Animus, the ancestors, Minerva
  and Juno, are referenced the way a person remembers their own life, not the way a wiki lists facts.
- Emotion is carried by small concrete moments (a leaf for the pain, a borrowed cloak), not by the
  narrator announcing feelings.
- Almost no choreography. Big events (touching the device, the golden tree) are rendered in short
  beats, not blow-by-blow.

## Excerpt

Desmond watched as they left. Shaun and Rebecca turned around one last time and Desmond grinned at them.

If this would be the last time they would see one another, Desmond wanted their last memory of him to be a nice one.

Once he was sure they left the Temple, Desmond turned to face the device once more. He could see Juno and Minerva standing a few feet away from him, on either side of him like some sort of pretentious angel-devil duo sitting on his shoulders.

Not that either of them was an angel.

They were both devils, giving different bad advice.

And all Desmond was doing was picking the lesser evil of the two.

Desmond took a deep breath and slowly reached out his hand to the device.

He could feel the way his right hand trembled.

Yet…

He felt peace.

This was the end of his journey.

His final act as Desmond Miles.

...

He touched the device.

And let out a blood-curdling scream as he felt the device start to burn him from the inside.

He screamed so loud that he didn't understand whatever it was that Minerva was saying.

A moment passed.

And everything went dark.

...

"Boy. Are you alright? Boy!"

Desmond gasped awake and he immediately rolled away from the voice, crouching as he used his arms to defend his face.

"It's okay. I'm not going to harm you."

Desmond blinked, recognizing the voice as speaking Arabic. Altaïr's antiquated Arabic, to be more precise.

He glanced around.

He was in some kind of narrow… Was it an alley? Probably.

But the buildings surrounding him… The clothes of the woman in front of him…

Shitshitshitshit.

The woman must have mistaken his growing panic and she knelt in front of him, placing her basket filled with a few pieces of flowers on the ground to her right. "Can you not understand me? Are you a Christian?"

She spoke in some kind of mangled French that Desmond barely understood thanks to Ezio's and Altaïr's memories.

"Not… hurt you."

He shook his head and took a deep breath. He needed to focus. He needed to be sure. He needed…

"… why am I naked?" Desmond realized with a high squeaking voice that cracked in the middle.

...

Desmond looked at his hands. His hands were smaller than he remembered.

He looked between his legs. Smooth. No hair at all.

Oh, fucking hell.

...

"And what's your name?" the woman asked as they slowly made their way out of the alley.

"Desmond…" Desmond paused for a moment. He took a deep breath as he said, "Desmond Ibn-La'Ahad."

The kind woman's understanding expression soothed him just a bit.

It was true. In this place… Here in the past… He knew he couldn't say he was Desmond Miles. Not when that name had too much connection to the future.

So, in the end… In this place, he found himself in… He was Desmond, son of no one.
